newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOCUS-Bulgaria sets new tender for 50,000T wheat.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bulgaria sets new tender for 50,000T wheat.

text.p: Bulgaria has called a tender to import 50,000 tonnes of wheat in exchange for exports from the new harvest after a previous tender failed, state news agency BTA said on Friday.
BTA quoted Agriculture Minister Roumen Hristov as saying the tender had to be held because Bulgarian trading firm Nada, which won a tender in March, did not fulfil its contractual obligations.

Hristov said after meeting Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski on Friday the interim cabinet would not import U.S. bread wheat under the U.S. Department of Agriculture's GSM-102 export credit guarantee programme as the price of more than $210 per tonne was too high.
He said negotiations would be held with Hungary, as the price would be $190 and delivery time would be much shorter.
Earlier this week, officials said Bulgaria needed about 100,000 tonnes of wheat to cover the gap until the new crop.
Another tender for importing 50,000 tonnes of wheat is expected to be called by the end of May but the terms are yet to be decided, officials said.
Both deals are to be guaranteed by the government through the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development through a stable state bank, probably the country's biggest, Bulbank.
Bulgaria received 100,000 tonnes of wheat from Poland in March to ease its grain shortage, against an agreement to export the same quantity of wheat from the new crop.
The country also awarded contracts to Swiss firm Glencore and to Nada to import 100,000 tonnes of wheat against forward contracts, but Hristov said Nada had not imported any grain.

Experts said the new crop, which is expected to be much better than last year's, will enable Bulgaria to meet its domestic needs, service export commitments under forward contracts and put aside wheat for the State Reserve.
The agricultural ministry forecasts 1997 wheat output at some 3.0 million tonnes, up from last year's 1.8 million tonnes. Bulgaria's domestic consumption is estimated at some 1.6 million tonnes.
Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year created acute grain shortages earlier this year, which have been overcome in the past three months.
Bulgaria sowed 1.5 million hectares with wheat and barley last year, up from 1.27 million hectares in the previous year.
